limitations: Hotspots are detections, not independent fires or burned area.
Cloud and overpass coverage are not measured. Missing observations are not zero fire activity.
Historical critical periods are not forecasts. Calendar bins start January 1, not ISO weeks.
The raw baseline switches instruments; it is a constructed comparison.
meta.no_observation_note: Days in a documented satellite outage, or with no detections in any of the seven countries, are shown as no observation and excluded from seasonal statistics and anomaly flags.
meta.extension_note: 2025 is converted S-NPP VIIRS beyond the validation period: the frozen M1 model is applied with no refitting. Calibration intervals are not computed for 2025. Weekly climatology, anomaly flags, critical periods, evaluation and the weekly rhythm results remain based on 2003-2024.

gate.label: REAL FIRMS DATA
reasons: Not enough matching, unflagged control results for US plus two other countries.
caveats: Hotspot detections are not independent fires or ignition events.
Cloud cover, satellite outages and overpass exposure are not measured by annual CSV availability.
A weekly association is consistent with human scheduling; it does not establish ignition cause.
Absence of a weekly dip does not establish weather-driven fire.
Terra, Aqua and VIIRS observe overlapping events; agreement is corroboration, not independent replication.
The null test assumes exchangeable weekday labels within each year under the null.
Static industrial sources may have real weekly schedules; controls are diagnostic, not a guaranteed natural null.
gate.rule: US and >=2 other countries each require >=2 streams with verified input years, rest day lowest, 95% upper bound <1 and fixed-family adjusted p<0.05; matching controls must be available and unflagged. Synthetic data never enable production.
